description: MariaDB MaxScale 25.10 configuration rendered to /etc/maxscale.cnf: one monitor, one readwritesplit service, one listener.

fields.name: threads
fields.description: Routing worker threads; `auto` means one per CPU core.
fields.title: Worker threads

fields.name: admin_host
fields.description: Address the REST API / GUI binds to; the default 127.0.0.1 keeps it local.
fields.title: Admin host

fields.name: admin_port
fields.description: Port of the REST API and the GUI.
fields.title: Admin port

fields.name: admin_secure_gui
fields.description: Serve the GUI over HTTPS only; turning it off needs admin_ssl_* to be unset.
fields.title: Secure GUI

fields.name: syslog
fields.description: Also write the log to syslog.
fields.title: Log to syslog

fields.name: maxlog
fields.description: Write MaxScale's own log file.
fields.title: Log to maxscale.log

fields.name: log_info
fields.description: Log at INFO level — useful while bringing a cluster up, noisy under load.
fields.title: Info logging

fields.name: monitor_module
fields.description: mariadbmon for asynchronous/semisync replication, galeramon for a Galera cluster.
fields.title: Monitor module

fields.name: monitor_user
fields.description: Backend account the monitor uses; needs REPLICATION CLIENT (and more for failover).
fields.title: Monitor user

fields.name: monitor_password
fields.description: Password of that account; filled by the server.
fields.title: Monitor password

fields.name: monitor_interval
fields.description: How often the monitor polls every backend. Rendered with an explicit ms suffix — unitless durations are deprecated.
fields.title: Monitor interval

fields.name: backend_timeout
fields.description: Connect, read and write timeout of one monitor check. Replaces the three backend_*_timeout parameters, which 25.10 deprecated.
fields.title: Backend timeout

fields.name: auto_failover
fields.description: Promote a replica when the primary is lost (mariadbmon only).
fields.title: Auto failover

fields.name: auto_rejoin
fields.description: Re-attach an old primary as a replica once it comes back (mariadbmon only).
fields.title: Auto rejoin

fields.name: enforce_read_only_slaves
fields.description: Set read_only=1 on any writable replica. The wider enforce_read_only_servers also exists — this is not a rename.
fields.title: Enforce read_only on replicas

fields.name: failcount
fields.description: Consecutive failed checks before the primary is declared down; 0 or 1 means immediately.
fields.title: Fail count

fields.name: replication_user
fields.description: Account written into CHANGE MASTER TO during failover/rejoin.
fields.title: Replication user

fields.name: replication_password
fields.description: Password of that account; filled by the server.
fields.title: Replication password

fields.name: cooperative_monitoring_locks
fields.description: Lets several MaxScale instances agree on who may run failover.
fields.title: Cooperative monitoring locks

fields.name: service_user
fields.description: Account MaxScale uses to read the backends' user tables.
fields.title: Service user

fields.name: service_password
fields.description: Password of that account; filled by the server.
fields.title: Service password

fields.name: master_accept_reads
fields.description: Send read traffic to the primary as well as the replicas.
fields.title: Primary accepts reads

fields.name: causal_reads
fields.description: Read-your-own-writes guarantee level; anything but none costs a synchronization wait.
fields.title: Causal reads

fields.name: causal_reads_timeout
fields.description: How long a causal read waits for the replica to catch up before it falls back to the primary.
fields.title: Causal reads timeout

fields.name: transaction_replay
fields.description: Replay an interrupted transaction on another server. Enabling it forces delayed_retry, master_reconnection and master_failure_mode=fail_on_write.
fields.title: Transaction replay

fields.name: transaction_replay_max_size
fields.description: Largest transaction MaxScale will buffer for replay.
fields.title: Transaction replay max size

fields.name: slave_selection_criteria
fields.description: How a read is assigned to a replica.
fields.title: Replica selection

fields.name: max_slave_connections
fields.description: How many replicas one session may hold connections to.
fields.title: Max replica connections

fields.name: max_replication_lag
fields.description: Replicas lagging more than this stop receiving reads; 0 disables the check. Whole seconds only.
fields.title: Max replication lag

fields.name: master_failure_mode
fields.description: What happens to a session when the primary disappears. 24.02 moved the default to fail_on_write, which is also what transaction_replay requires.
fields.title: Primary failure mode

fields.name: transaction_replay_timeout
fields.description: How long MaxScale keeps retrying a replayed transaction before giving up; 0 falls back to the session's own timeouts.
fields.title: Transaction replay timeout

fields.name: listener_port
fields.description: Port clients connect to.
fields.title: Listener port

fields.name: listener_address
fields.description: Address the listener binds to; :: means every interface.
fields.title: Listener address

fields.name: listener_protocol
fields.description: Client protocol module. This is the only place `protocol` is valid — a [server] section has none.
fields.title: Listener protocol

fields.name: servers
fields.description: The [server] sections plus the servers= lists of the monitor and the service; filled by the server from topology.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the [server] section, e.g. db-1.
fields.title: Section name

fields.name: address
fields.description: Backend host or IP.
fields.title: Address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Backend port.
fields.title: Port

fields.name: priority
fields.description: galeramon only: lower wins when use_priority is on. Ignored by mariadbmon.
fields.title: Priority
Backends

fields.name: custom
fields.description: Raw `key = value` settings appended verbatim at the end of the file; keys must match ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_.]*$. Entry order is not preserved.
fields.title: Extra settings

fields.name: server_sections
fields.description: One [server] section per backend — with no protocol parameter, which MaxScale does not accept there.

computed.expr:
(("servers" in root) && size(root.servers) > 0) ? root.servers.map(s,
					"[" + string(s.name) + "]
type=server
address=" + string(s.address) +
					"
port=" + (("port" in s) ? string(s.port) : "3306") + "
priority=" + (("priority" in s) ? string(s.priority) : "0") + "
").join("
") : ""

fields.title: Server sections

fields.name: server_names
fields.description: Comma-separated section names for the monitor's and the service's servers= lines.
fields.title: Server names

fields.name: monitor_extra
fields.description: The mariadbmon-only failover parameters, or galeramon's use_priority.

computed.expr:
(root.monitor_module == "mariadbmon") ?
					("auto_failover=" + string(root.auto_failover) +
					"\nauto_rejoin=" + string(root.auto_rejoin) +
					"\nenforce_read_only_slaves=" + string(root.enforce_read_only_slaves) +
					"\nfailcount=" + string(root.failcount) +
					"\nreplication_user=" + string(root.replication_user) +
					"\nreplication_password=" + (("replication_password" in root) ? string(root.replication_password) : "") +
					"\ncooperative_monitoring_locks=" + string(root.cooperative_monitoring_locks) + "\n")
					: "use_priority=true\n"

fields.title: Monitor extras

fields.name: custom_rendered
fields.description: The `custom` map joined into extra key=value lines of the [rwsplit-service] section.
fields.title: Rendered extra service parameters

rules.expr: !("transaction_replay" in root) || root.transaction_replay != "true" || !("master_failure_mode" in root) || root.master_failure_mode == "fail_on_write"
rules.message: transaction_replay forces master_failure_mode=fail_on_write — set it explicitly

rules.expr: !("monitor_module" in root) || root.monitor_module != "galeramon" || !("auto_failover" in root) || root.auto_failover == "false"
rules.message: auto_failover is a mariadbmon parameter; galeramon has no failover

rules.expr: !("causal_reads_timeout" in root) || !("monitor_interval" in root) || int(root.causal_reads_timeout) >= int(root.monitor_interval)
rules.message: causal_reads_timeout below monitor_interval makes causal reads fail before the monitor notices anything
